newsitem.title: UK: UK's Clarke says does not need to raise tax.
newsitem.headline: UK's Clarke says does not need to raise tax.

text.p: Chancellor of the Exchequer Kenneth Clarke said on Wednesday he did not need to raise tax to carry out the government's spending plans.
"I don't need to raise taxes. I've got my spending plans. I've been reducing taxation. I have clearly committed this government to a course which we can deliver," he told BBC radio in an interview.

Clarke was speaking shortly after the Conservative Party unveiled its manifesto for the May 1 election which promises tax breaks for people who stayed at home to take care of childen or sick relatives.
Prime Minister John Major said at the launch he could not envisage any situation in which tax would have to rise.

"I cannot conceive, except in the most exceptional circumstances that cannot be forseen at the moment, that we would need to increase general tax levels in the next Parliament given our public expenditure plands and outlook for the economy," Major said.
